definition: The Global Index on Responsible AI (GIRAI) is a study that scores countries on national policies, human rights, and institutional capacity related to artificial intelligence (AI) and it is produced by the Global Center on AI Governance, a South African-based research organization.
details: The Global Index on Responsible AI (GIRAI) is a study that scores countries on national policies, human rights, and institutional capacity related to artificial intelligence (AI) and it is produced by the Global Center on AI Governance, a South African-based research organization.

explainer.lead: The Global Index on Responsible AI, or GIRAI, is a country-level study of national AI policies, human rights, and institutional capacity. Produced by the South African-based Global Center on AI Governance, it gives countries scores that make their approaches to responsible AI easier to compare.

tiers.eli5: Think of GIRAI as a report card for how a country handles AI. Instead of grading one app or robot, it looks at the country's rules, its treatment of people's rights, and whether its institutions are equipped to do the work. The scores help people compare different countries.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer or policy team can use GIRAI as country-level context when examining the governance environment around an AI system. Its assessment areas are national policies, human rights, and institutional capacity. A country score is not a substitute for product testing, legal review, or evaluation of an individual model.
tiers.paperLevel: Let GIRAI(c) denote the index score for country c, based on national policies P(c), human rights H(c), and institutional capacity I(c): GIRAI(c) = F(P(c), H(c), I(c)). The unit of analysis is national AI governance, not the accuracy or safety of an individual AI model.

explainer.example: Consider a hypothetical country that has a national AI policy but limited institutional capacity. GIRAI would not assess the written policy alone: it would also examine human rights and institutional capacity before assigning the country's score.

usedIn.name: Comparative AI governance
usedIn.detail: Provides a common frame for comparing countries' national approaches to responsible AI.

usedIn.name: Human-rights research
usedIn.detail: Places human rights alongside policy and institutional capacity in country-level AI assessment.

usedIn.name: AI policy analysis
usedIn.detail: Helps researchers examine national AI policies together with the institutions responsible for governance.

explainer.intuition: GIRAI treats responsible AI as a feature of a country's governance environment, not just of its technology. It brings rules, rights, and institutional capacity into one comparative study.
howItWorks: Take a country as the unit of assessment.
Examine its national policies related to AI.
Assess human rights in relation to AI.
Examine the country's institutional capacity for AI governance.
Use these assessments to produce country scores for the index.
explainer.whyItMatters: GIRAI gives researchers and policymakers a shared way to compare national AI governance. Looking at policies, rights, and capacity together can reveal differences that a count of AI strategies or laws would miss.
misconceptions: GIRAI does not rank AI models, products, or companies; it scores countries.
A national AI policy by itself does not determine a country's assessment.
A country score does not establish that every AI system used there is safe or responsible.
